shared_context.chief_complaint: dysphagia, slurred speech, coughing on liquids for 3 months

atoms.1: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and slurred speech may indicate a neuromuscular disorder.
atoms.2: The patient's past coughing when drinking liquids suggests a disorder of the central or peripheral nervous system.
atoms.3: Slurred speech suggests a disorder of the central or peripheral nervous system.
atoms.4: These symptoms (coughing when drinking liquids and slurred speech) can lead to aspiration.
atoms.5: No significant medical history makes it less likely that the symptoms are due to a secondary cause.
atoms.6: A secondary cause could be a medication side effect or another medical condition.
atoms.7: The lack of fever, normal blood pressure, and normal pulse and respirations make an infectious or acute inflammatory cause less likely.
atoms.8: These physical exam findings suggest a disorder of the lower motor neuron.
atoms.9: No sensory deficits support a lower motor neuron disorder.
atoms.10: The most likely diagnosis is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
atoms.11: ALS is a motor neuron disease.
atoms.12: ALS is characterized by the progressive degeneration of both upper and lower motor neurons.
atoms.13: Given the diagnosis of ALS, the best therapy for improving survival is Riluzole.
atoms.14: Riluzole is the only FDA-approved medication for ALS.
atoms.15: Riluzole has been shown to prolong survival by an average of 2-3 months.
